title: Genetic Engineering of Novel Yellow Color African Violet (Saintpaulia ionantha)
author: Rajabi, Fahmideh, et al.
materials: Total DNA was extracted from fresh petal of putative transgenic plants with CTAB method as previously described [44]. For PCR analysis, p1 and p2 specific primers were used for 4’CGT and AS1 genes (Supplementary Table S2). PCR was performed using GoTaq® Green Master Mix (Promega, Madison, WI, USA) in a T100 thermal cycle (Bio-Rad), with initial denaturation at 95 ºC for 5 min, followed by 35 cycles at 95 ºC for 45 s, 58 ºC for 30 s and 72 ºC for 2 min, and a final extension step at 72 ºC for 10 min. The analysis of products was performed via 1% agarose gel electrophoresis and sequencing (Sanger Sequencing method, ABI 3730 XL).

For Southern blot analysis, genomic DNA of petals was treated with 10 µg L−1 RNase for 4 h at 25 °C, followed by phenol-chloroform extraction and ethanol precipitation. Representative probes were prepared with digoxigenin, by used DIG DNA labeling and detection kit. 30 µg DNA of each leaves sample was cut with NcoI enzyme for AS1 and BamHI enzyme for 4CGT (Thermo Fisher) by incubating for 16 h at 37 °C. The digested products were separated by 1% agarose gel, denatured in 1.5 M NaCl, 0.5 M NaOH for 30 min each, and transferred to hybridization membrane (GeneScreen, DuPont, Boston, MA, USA). Hybridization was performed at 65 °C with digoxigenin-labeled probe (Amersham Rediprim II, GE Healthcare, Pittsburgh, PA, USA). After 20 h of hybridization, the membrane was washed twice in 2× SSC at room temperature for 15 min each, twice in 2× SSC, 1% SDS at 65 °C for 30 min each, and finally once in 0.1× SSC at room temperature for 30 min. The membrane was exposed to an imaging plate at room temperature and the signal was detected by a phosphor imager (Typhoon FLA 7000, GE Healthcare, Pittsburgh, PA, USA).

For real-time quantitative PCR, total RNA was extracted from African violet white (non-transformation), transgenic A. violet, and A. majus petals all treated with DNase I, as previously described by wang et al. [45]. Next, cDNA was synthesized from total RNA (100 ng) using the Superscript III First-Strand Synthesis System (Invitrogen, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA) and oligo (dT) 20. The transcript levels of 4’CGT and AS1 were analyzed via RT-qPCR (Applied Biosystems 7900HT Fast Real-Time PCR System) using Power SYBRTM Green PCR Master Mix (Applied Biosystems, Thermo Fisher Scientific) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Transcript levels were calculated based on ∆∆Cq (formerly ∆∆Ct) method [46] using Actin (accession number: AB596843.1) gene as references. Statistical significance of the differential expression levels was assessed as independent experiments (with mean centering and autoscaling) [47]. The Tukey–Kramer test at the 1% level was used for the analysis of aurone biosynthesis-related genes. The results are presented as the standardized mean of SE.

steps.title: Extract genomic DNA from petals
steps.instruction: Extract total DNA from fresh petal tissue of putative transgenic African violet plants using the CTAB method as described previously.

steps.title: Amplify 4’CGT and AS1 by PCR
steps.instruction: Set up PCR reactions with GoTaq® Green Master Mix (Promega) using p1 and p2 primers (Supplementary Table S2) for the 4’CGT and AS1 genes, then run on a Bio‑Rad T100 thermal cycler with the following program: 95 °C 5 min initial denaturation; 35 cycles of 95 °C 45 s, 58 °C 30 s, 72 °C 2 min; final extension 72 °C 10 min.

steps.title: Analyze PCR products
steps.instruction: Separate PCR amplicons on a 1 % agarose gel, visualize the bands, and send the products for Sanger sequencing on an ABI 3730 XL instrument.

steps.title: Prepare DNA for Southern blot
steps.instruction: Treat the extracted genomic DNA with RNase (10 µg L⁻¹) for 4 h at 25 °C, then perform phenol‑chloroform extraction followed by ethanol precipitation.

steps.title: Digest DNA with restriction enzymes
steps.instruction: Take 30 µg of each DNA sample and digest with NcoI (for AS1) or BamHI (for 4’CGT) (Thermo Fisher) by incubating for 16 h at 37 °C.

steps.title: Separate and denature digested DNA
steps.instruction: Run the digested DNA on a 1 % agarose gel, then denature the gel slices in 1.5 M NaCl and 0.5 M NaOH for 30 min each.

steps.title: Transfer DNA to membrane
steps.instruction: Transfer the denatured DNA fragments onto a GeneScreen hybridization membrane (DuPont, Boston, MA, USA).

steps.title: Hybridize with DIG‑labeled probe
steps.instruction: Hybridize the membrane at 65 °C with a digoxigenin‑labeled probe prepared using the DIG DNA labeling and detection kit (Amersham Rediprim II, GE Healthcare) for 20 h.

steps.title: Wash membrane post‑hybridization
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane as follows: twice in 2× SSC at room temperature for 15 min each; twice in 2× SSC + 1 % SDS at 65 °C for 30 min each; once in 0.1× SSC at room temperature for 30 min.

steps.title: Detect Southern blot signal
steps.instruction: Expose the washed membrane to an imaging plate at room temperature and capture the signal with a Typhoon FLA 7000 phosphor imager (GE Healthcare, Pittsburgh, PA, USA).

steps.title: Extract total RNA for qRT‑PCR
steps.instruction: Extract total RNA from African violet white (non‑transformed), transgenic A. violet, and A. majus petals, treating the extracts with DNase I as described by Wang et al. (ref 45).

steps.title: Synthesize cDNA
steps.instruction: Use 100 ng of each RNA sample to synthesize first‑strand cDNA with the Superscript III First‑Strand Synthesis System (Invitrogen, Thermo Fisher) and oligo(dT)20 primers.

steps.title: Perform quantitative RT‑PCR
steps.instruction: Run RT‑qPCR on an Applied Biosystems 7900HT Fast Real‑Time PCR System using Power SYBR Green PCR Master Mix (Applied Biosystems). Amplify 4’CGT, AS1, and Actin (reference gene, accession AB596843.1) according to the manufacturer’s protocol, and calculate relative expression by the ΔΔCq method.

steps.title: Prepare petal sections for light microscopy
steps.instruction: Cut petals into 5 × 5 mm pieces, embed them in 4 % agarose, and cut 100 µm thick sections with a Micro Slicer DTK‑1000 (D.S.K.). Examine the sections under a VH‑Z75 light microscope (Keyence).
